questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two spheres are projected at angles $30^{}^{\circ}$ and $45^{}^{\circ}$ with the horizontal. The maximum height reached by both is same. The ratio of their initial velocities is, $\left(\sin 45^{}^{\circ} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, \sin 30^{}^{\circ} = 0.5\right)$
questions.solution:
The maximum height reached by a projectile is given by $H = \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2 \theta}{2g}$

Given that the maximum heights are equal for both spheres:

$H_1 = H_2$

$\dfrac{u_1^2 \sin^2 \theta_1}{2g} = \dfrac{u_2^2 \sin^2 \theta_2}{2g}$

$u_1 \sin \theta_1 = u_2 \sin \theta_2$

Substituting $\theta_1 = 30^{}^{\circ}$ and $\theta_2 = 45^{}^{\circ}$:

$u_1 \sin 30^{}^{\circ} = u_2 \sin 45^{}^{\circ}$

$u_1 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) =u_2 \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)

\dfrac{u_1}{u_2} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{1}

The ratio of their initial velocities is \sqrt{2}$: 1$.

Answer: \sqrt{2}$: 1

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A car is travelling at 40 m/s on a circular path of radius 40 m. It is increasing its speed at the rate of $2\ \text{m/s}^2$. Its net acceleration is (in $\text{m/s}^2$) nearly
questions.solution:
Given $v = 40\ \text{m/s}$ and $R = 40\ \text{m}$.

Tangential acceleration, $a_t = 2\ \text{m/s}^2$.

Centripetal acceleration, $a_c = \dfrac{v^2}{R} = \dfrac{40^2}{40} = 40\ \text{m/s}^2$.

Net acceleration, $a = \sqrt{a_c^2 + a_t^2} = \sqrt{40^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt{1600 + 4} = \sqrt{1604} \approx 40\ \text{m/s}^2$.

Answer: $40\ \text{m/s}^2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle completes 2 revolutions in a circular path of radius 3 cm. The angular displacement of the particle will be (in radian)
questions.solution:
Angular displacement for one complete revolution is $2\pi$ radians.

For $2$ complete revolutions, the angular displacement is given by $\theta = 2 \times 2\pi = 4\pi$ radians.

The radius of the circular path does not affect the angular displacement.

Answer: $4\pi$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The equation of the trajectory of a ball projected at an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal, is given as $y = x - \dfrac{gx^2}{2}$
The initial velocity of the ball is
[Given : $\tan 45^{}^{\circ} = 1$, $\cos 45^{}^{\circ} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ ]
questions.solution:
The standard equation of trajectory of a projectile is given by

$y = x \tan \theta - \dfrac{gx^2}{2u^2 \cos^2 \theta}$

Comparing this with the given equation $y = x - \dfrac{gx^2}{2}$, we get

$\tan \theta = 1 \Rightarrow \theta = 45^{}^{\circ}$

and

$\dfrac{g}{2u^2 \cos^2 \theta} = \dfrac{g}{2}$

$u^2 \cos^2 \theta = 1$

Substituting $\theta = 45^{}^{\circ}$,

$u^2 \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 = 1$

$\dfrac{u^2}{2} = 1$

$u^2 = 2$

$u = \sqrt{2} \text{ m/s}$

Answer: $\sqrt{2}\,\text{m/s}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle is performing U.C.M. along a circle of radius $R$. In half the period of revolution, its displacement and distance covered are respectively
questions.solution:
In half the period of revolution, the particle moves from its initial position to the diametrically opposite point on the circular path.

The displacement is the shortest distance between the initial and final positions, which is equal to the diameter of the circle.

Displacement = $2R$

The distance covered is the actual path length along the circular trajectory, which is half of the circumference.

Distance = $\dfrac{2\pi R}{2} = \pi R$

Answer: $2R, \pi R$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two particles having mass 'M' and 'm' are moving in a circular path with radius 'R' and 'r' respectively. The time period for both the particles is same. The ratio of angular velocity of the first particle to that of the second particle will be
questions.solution:
Angular velocity is given by $\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T}$

Since the time period $T$ is the same for both particles, their angular velocities are equal.

$\omega_1 = \dfrac{2\pi}{T}$ and $\omega_2 = \dfrac{2\pi}{T}$

$\dfrac{\omega_1}{\omega_2} = \dfrac{1}{1}$

The ratio of their angular velocities is $1:1$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two stones of masses $m$ and $3m$ are whirled in horizontal circles, the heavier one in a radius $\dfrac{r}{3}$ and the lighter one in radius $r$. When both the stones experience same centripetal forces, the tangential speed of lighter stone is '$n$' times that of the value of heavier stone. The value of '$n$' is
questions.solution:
Let the mass, radius, and tangential speed of the lighter stone be $m_1 = m$, $r_1 = r$, and $v_1$ respectively.

Let the mass, radius, and tangential speed of the heavier stone be $m_2 = 3m$, $r_2 = \dfrac{r}{3}$, and $v_2$ respectively.

The centripetal force on the lighter stone is $F_1 = \dfrac{m_1 v_1^2}{r_1} = \dfrac{m v_1^2}{r}$.

The centripetal force on the heavier stone is $F_2 = \dfrac{m_2 v_2^2}{r_2} = \dfrac{3m v_2^2}{\dfrac{r}{3}} = \dfrac{9m v_2^2}{r}$.

Given that both stones experience the same centripetal force, $F_1 = F_2$.

$\dfrac{m v_1^2}{r} = \dfrac{9m v_2^2}{r}$

$v_1^2 = 9 v_2^2$

$v_1 = 3 v_2$

Since the tangential speed of the lighter stone is $n$ times that of the heavier stone, $n = 3$.

Answer: $3$

questions.q: For a projectile motion, the range R is 'n' times the maximum height H. So the angle of projection is
questions.solution: The horizontal range $R$ of a projectile is given by$R = \dfrac{u^2 \sin 2\theta}{g} = \dfrac{2u^2 \sin\theta \cos\theta}{g}$The maximum height $H$ is given by$H = \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g}$Given that $R = nH$, substituting the expressions for $R$ and $H \dfrac{2u^2 \sin\theta \cos\theta}{g} = n  \left( \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g} \right)Cancelling \dfrac{u^2 \sin\theta}{g} from both sides2 \cos$\theta = $\dfrac{n \sin\theta}{2}  \dfrac{$\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ = \dfrac{4}{n}$\tan$\theta = $$\dfrac{4}{n}$  \theta = $\tan^{-1}$$\$left($\dfrac{4}{n}$\right)$Answer: \tan^{-1} $\$left(\dfrac{4}{n}\right)$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body moves along a circular path of diameter $30\ \text{cm}$. It starts from one end of diameter, moves along the circular path and reaches the other end of diameter in 3 second. The angular speed of the body in radian per second is
questions.solution:
The angular displacement of the body when it moves from one end of the diameter to the other end along the circular path is $\pi$ radians.

Time taken, $t = 3\ \text{s}$.

Angular speed, $\omega = \dfrac{\theta}{t}$

$\omega = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\ \text{rad/s}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A ball P is projected at an angle of $60^{}^{\circ}$ with the vertical with certain initial speed. Another ball Q of the same mass as that of ball P is projected vertically upwards with the same initial speed as that of P. At the highest point, the ratio of potential energy of ball P to that of ball Q is
$(\sin 30^{}^{\circ} = 0.5)$
questions.solution:
Let the initial speed of both balls be $u$ and their mass be $m$.

For ball P, the angle of projection with the vertical is $60^{}^{\circ}$, so the angle with the horizontal is $\theta_P = 90^{}^{\circ} - 60^{}^{\circ} = 30^{}^{\circ}$.

The maximum height reached by ball P is $H_P = \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2 30^{}^{\circ}}{2g} = \dfrac{u^2 (1/2)^2}{2g} = \dfrac{u^2}{8g}$.

The potential energy of ball P at the highest point is $U_P = mgH_P = mg \left(\dfrac{u^2}{8g}\right) = \dfrac{mu^2}{8}$.

For ball Q, it is projected vertically upwards, so the angle of projection with the horizontal is $\theta_Q = 90^{}^{\circ}$.

The maximum height reached by ball Q is $H_Q = \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2 90^{}^{\circ}}{2g} = \dfrac{u^2}{2g}$.

The potential energy of ball Q at the highest point is $U_Q = mgH_Q = mg \left(\dfrac{u^2}{2g}\right) = \dfrac{mu^2}{2}$.

The ratio of their potential energies at the highest point is $\dfrac{U_P}{U_Q} = \dfrac{\dfrac{mu^2}{8}}{\dfrac{mu^2}{2}} = \dfrac{2}{8} = \dfrac{1}{4}$.

Answer: $1 : 4$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Two balls A and B are projected at an angle of $45^{}^{\circ}$ and $60^{}^{\circ}$ respectively, so that the maximum heights reached are same for both. The ratio of initial velocity of projection of ball A to that for ball B is
$(\sin 30^{}^{\circ} = \cos 60^{}^{\circ} = \dfrac{1}{2},\ \sin 45^{}^{\circ} = \cos 45^{}^{\circ} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}},\ \sin 60^{}^{\circ} = \cos 30^{}^{\circ} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2})$
questions.solution:
The maximum height reached by a projectile is given by $H = \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2 \theta}{2g}$

For ball A, $H_A = \dfrac{u_A^2 \sin^2 45^{}^{\circ}}{2g}$

For ball B, $H_B = \dfrac{u_B^2 \sin^2 60^{}^{\circ}}{2g}$

Since $H_A = H_B$, we have:

$\dfrac{u_A^2 \sin^2 45^{}^{\circ}}{2g} = \dfrac{u_B^2 \sin^2 60^{}^{\circ}}{2g}$

$u_A \sin 45^{}^{\circ} = u_B \sin 60^{}^{\circ}$

$\dfrac{u_A}{u_B} = \dfrac{\sin 60^{}^{\circ}}{\sin 45^{}^{\circ}}$

Substituting the values $\sin 60^{}^{\circ} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ and $\sin 45^{}^{\circ} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$:

$\dfrac{u_A}{u_B} = \dfrac{\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{2}}$

The ratio of initial velocity of projection of ball A to that for ball B is $\sqrt{3} : \sqrt{2}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two objects are projected with same velocity 'u' at different angles $\alpha$ and $\beta$ with the horizontal. If $\alpha + \beta = 90^{}^{\circ}$, the ratio of horizontal range of the first object to the second object will be $[\sin(\pi - \theta) = \sin\theta]$
questions.solution:
The horizontal range of a projectile is given by $R = \dfrac{u^2 \sin(2\theta)}{g}$.

For the first object projected at angle $\alpha$, the range is $R_1 = \dfrac{u^2 \sin(2\alpha)}{g}$.

For the second object projected at angle $\beta$, the range is $R_2 = \dfrac{u^2 \sin(2\beta)}{g}$.

Given $\alpha + \beta = 90^{}^{\circ}$, we have $\beta = 90^{}^{\circ} - \alpha$.

Substituting $\beta$ in the expression for $R_2$:

$R_2 = \dfrac{u^2 \sin(2(90^{}^{\circ} - \alpha))}{g} = \dfrac{u^2 \sin(180^{}^{\circ} - 2\alpha)}{g}$

Using the identity $\sin(180^{}^{\circ} - \theta) = \sin\theta$, we get:

$R_2 = \dfrac{u^2 \sin(2\alpha)}{g}$

Thus, $R_1 = R_2$, which means the ratio of their horizontal ranges is $1 : 1$.

Answer: $1 : 1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle describes a horizontal circle of radius 'r' in conical funnel with smooth inner surface with a speed of $0.5$ m/s. The height of the plane of the circle from the vertex of the funnel is (acceleration due to gravity, $g = 10\,\text{m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
Let $\theta$ be the semi-vertical angle of the conical funnel.
The radius of the circular path is $r$ and its height from the vertex is $h$.
From the geometry of the cone, we have:
$\tan \theta = \dfrac{r}{h}$

The forces acting on the particle are its weight $mg$ acting vertically downwards and the normal reaction $N$ acting perpendicular to the inner surface of the funnel.
The normal reaction makes an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal. Resolving $N$ into vertical and horizontal components, we get:
$N \sin \theta = mg$
$N \cos \theta = \dfrac{mv^2}{r}$

Dividing the vertical component by the horizontal component, we obtain:
$\tan \theta = \dfrac{rg}{v^2}$

Equating the two expressions for $\tan \theta$:
$\dfrac{r}{h} = \dfrac{rg}{v^2}$

$\Rightarrow h = \dfrac{v^2}{g}$

Given $v = 0.5$ m/s and $g = 10$ m/s$^2$, substituting the values:
$h = \dfrac{(0.5)^2}{10} = \dfrac{0.25}{10} = 0.025$ m

Converting to centimeters:
$h = 0.025 \times 100$ cm $= 2.5$ cm

Answer: $2.5$ cm

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle is moving with constant angular acceleration $4\,\text{rad/s}^2$ in circular path. At what time the magnitudes of its tangential acceleration and centripetal acceleration will be equal ?
questions.solution:
Given angular acceleration $\alpha = 4 \text{ rad/s}^2$.

Tangential acceleration is given by $a_t = r\alpha$.

Centripetal acceleration is given by $a_c = r\omega^2$.

Equating the magnitudes of tangential and centripetal acceleration:

$a_t = a_c$

$r\alpha = r\omega^2$

$\omega^2 = \alpha$

Assuming the particle starts from rest, the angular velocity at time $t$ is $\omega = \alpha t$.

Substituting $\omega$ in the above equation:

$(\alpha t)^2 = \alpha$

$\alpha^2 t^2 = \alpha$

$t^2 = \dfrac{1}{\alpha}$

Substituting $\alpha = 4 \text{ rad/s}^2$:

$t^2 = \dfrac{1}{4}$

$t = 0.5 \text{ s}$

Answer: $0.5$ s

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two boys are standing at points A and B on ground where distance AB = a. The boy at point B starts running perpendicular to line AB with velocity '$V_1$'. The boy at point A starts running simultaneously with velocity 'V' and catches the other boy in time 't'. The value of 't' is
questions.solution:
Let the meeting point be C.

In the right-angled triangle ABC, the initial distance AB is $a$.

Since the boy at B runs perpendicular to AB, the angle at B is $90^{{}^{\circ}}$.

The distance travelled by the boy from B is $BC = V_1 t$.

The distance travelled by the boy from A is $AC = V t$.

Using Pythagoras theorem in $\triangle ABC$:

$(AC)^2 = (AB)^2 + (BC)^2$

$(V t)^2 = a^2 + (V_1 t)^2$

$V^2 t^2 - V_1^2 t^2 = a^2$

$t^2 (V^2 - V_1^2) = a^2$

$t = \left[\dfrac{a^2}{V^2 - V_1^2}\right]^{\dfrac{1}{2}}$

Answer: $\left[\dfrac{a^2}{(V^2 - V_1^2)}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle at rest starts moving with constant angular acceleration '$\alpha$' in a circular path of radius 'r'. At certain instant, the magnitude of centripetal acceleration is $\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^{rd}$ the tangential acceleration. The relation between linear speed (V) and angular acceleration ($\alpha$) is
questions.solution:
The tangential acceleration of the particle is given by $a_t = r\alpha$.

The centripetal acceleration of the particle is given by $a_c = \dfrac{V^2}{r}$.

According to the given condition, the magnitude of centripetal acceleration is $\dfrac{1}{3}$ of the tangential acceleration:

$a_c = \dfrac{1}{3} a_t$

Substituting the expressions for $a_c$ and $a_t$:

$\dfrac{V^2}{r} = \dfrac{1}{3} (r\alpha)$

$V^2 = \dfrac{r^2 \alpha}{3}$

Taking the square root on both sides:

$V = r\sqrt{\dfrac{\alpha}{3}}$

Answer: $V = r\sqrt{\dfrac{\alpha}{3}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A batsman hits a ball with a velocity 'v', making an angle of $60^{}^{\circ}$ with the vertical. After some time direction of velocity is making an angle of $60^{}^{\circ}$ with the horizontal. The speed of the ball at this instant is
$\left[\cos(60^{}^{\circ}) = \dfrac{1}{2}, \cos(30^{}^{\circ}) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right]$
questions.solution:
The initial angle of the velocity with the vertical is $60^{}^{\circ}$. Therefore, the initial angle with the horizontal is $90^{}^{\circ} - 60^{}^{\circ} = 30^{}^{\circ}$.

The horizontal component of the initial velocity is $u_x = v \cos(30^{}^{\circ})$.

Let the speed of the ball be $v'$ when its direction of motion makes an angle of $60^{}^{\circ}$ with the horizontal. The horizontal component of velocity at this instant is $v'_x = v' \cos(60^{}^{\circ})$.

In projectile motion, the horizontal component of velocity remains constant throughout the flight.

Equating the horizontal components of velocity:

$v' \cos(60^{}^{\circ}) = v \cos(30^{}^{\circ})$

Substituting the given trigonometric values:

$v' \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) =v \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)

$v' = $\sqrt{3} v$

Answer: $\sqrt{3} v$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: $A particle performing U.C.M. of radius \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ m makes 'x' revolutions in time t. Its tangential velocity is
questions.solution:
The radius of the circular path is $r = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ m.

The particle makes $x$ revolutions in time $t$, so its frequency is $n = \dfrac{x}{t}$.

The angular velocity is given by $\omega = 2\pi n = \dfrac{2\pi x}{t}$.

The tangential velocity is $v = r\omega$.

Substituting the values, we get $v = \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) \left(\dfrac{2\pi x}{t}\right) = \dfrac{\pi^2 x}{t}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi^2 x}{t}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: $A string of length 'L' fixed at one end carries a mass 'm' at the other end. The string makes \dfrac{3}{\pi}$ r.p.s. around the vertical axis through fixed end. The tension in the string is
questions.solution:
For a mass rotating in a horizontal circle as a conical pendulum, the horizontal component of the tension provides the necessary centripetal force.

$T \sin \theta = m \omega^2 r$

From the geometry of the pendulum, the radius of the circular path is $r = L \sin \theta$. Substituting this into the equation gives:

$T \sin \theta = m \omega^2 (L \sin \theta)$

$T = m \omega^2 L$

The frequency of revolution is given as $f = \dfrac{3}{\pi}$. The angular velocity $\omega$ is:

$\omega = 2 \pi f = 2 \pi \left( \dfrac{3}{\pi} \right) = 6$

Substituting the value of $\omega$ into the expression for tension:

$T = m (6)^2 L = 36 mL$

Answer: $36 mL$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In non uniform circular motion, the ratio of radial acceleration to tangential acceleration is (V is the velocity, r is the radius and $\alpha$ is the angular acceleration)
questions.solution:
Radial acceleration is given by $a_r = \dfrac{V^2}{r}$

Tangential acceleration is given by $a_t = r\alpha$

The ratio of radial acceleration to tangential acceleration is $\dfrac{a_r}{a_t} = \dfrac{\dfrac{V^2}{r}}{r\alpha} = \dfrac{V^2}{r^2\alpha}$

Answer: $\dfrac{V^2}{r^2\alpha}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The angular speed of the minute hand of a clock in degrees per second is
questions.solution:
The minute hand of a clock completes one full revolution in $1$ hour.

Total angle covered in one revolution is $360^{{}^{\circ}}$.

Total time taken is $1 \text{ hour} = 3600 \text{ seconds}$.

Angular speed $\omega = \dfrac{360^{{}^{\circ}}}{3600 \text{ s}} = 0.1^{{}^{\circ}} \text{/s}$

Answer: $0.1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The position vector of a particle is $\vec{r} = a \cos \omega t \hat{i} + a \sin \omega t \hat{j}$. Calculate the angle between its position vector and the velocity vector.
(\cos 0=1, \cos 90=0, \cos 60=0.5, \sin 30=0.5, \sin 0=0$)$
questions.solution:
Given position vector $\vec{r} = a \cos \omega t \hat{i} + a \sin \omega t \hat{j}$

Velocity vector $\vec{v} = \dfrac{d\vec{r}}{dt} = -a \omega \sin \omega t \hat{i} + a \omega \cos \omega t \hat{j}$

The dot product of $\vec{r}$ and $\vec{v}$ is:

$\vec{r} \cdot \vec{v} = (a \cos \omega t)(-a \omega \sin \omega t) + (a \sin \omega t)(a \omega \cos \omega t)$

$\vec{r} \cdot \vec{v} = -a^2 \omega \sin \omega t \cos \omega t + a^2 \omega \sin \omega t \cos \omega t = 0$

Since $\vec{r} \cdot \vec{v} = 0$, the angle between the position vector and the velocity vector is $90^{}^{\circ}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle of mass $m$ is moving in a circular path of constant radius $r$ such that its centripetal acceleration $a_c$ is varying with time $t$ as, $a_c = k^2 r t^2$. The power delivered to the particle by the forces acting on it is (K$ = constant)$
questions.solution:
Given centripetal acceleration $a_c = k^2 r t^2$

Using the formula $a_c = \dfrac{v^2}{r}$:

$\dfrac{v^2}{r} = k^2 r t^2$

$v^2 = k^2 r^2 t^2$

$v = k r t$

The kinetic energy of the particle is given by:

$E = \dfrac{1}{2} m v^2$

$E = \dfrac{1}{2} m (k r t)^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} m k^2 r^2 t^2$

The total power delivered by all forces acting on the particle is equal to the rate of change of its kinetic energy:

$P = \dfrac{dE}{dt}$

$P = \dfrac{d}{dt} \left( \dfrac{1}{2}$ m k² r² t² \right)$

$P = $\dfrac{1}{2}$ m k² r² (2t)$

$P = m k² r² t$$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two girls are standing at the ends 'A' and 'B' of a ground where $A B=b$. The girl at ' $B$ ' starts running in a direction perpendicular to ' AB ' with velocity ' $\mathrm{V}_1$ '. The girl at 'A' starts running simultaneously with velocity ' $\mathrm{V}_2$ ' and in shortest distance meets the other girl in time ' t '. The value of ' $t$ ' is
questions.solution:
Establish a coordinate system where girl A starts at $(0,0)$ and girl B at $(b,0)$. Girl B runs perpendicular to AB with velocity $V_1$, placing her position at time $t$ at $(b, V_1 t)$.

Girl A runs directly toward this meeting point with velocity $V_2$. The distance traveled by A is the straight-line distance between initial positions, given by the Pythagorean theorem:

$(V_2 t)^2 = b^2 + (V_1 t)^2$

Solving for $t$:

$V_2^2 t^2 - V_1^2 t^2 = b^2$
$t^2 (V_2^2 - V_1^2) = b^2$
$t = \frac{b}{\sqrt{V_2^2 - V_1^2}}$

This solution requires $V_2 > V_1$ for real $t$. The expression matches option D.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{D}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two boys are standing at points $A$ and $B$ on ground, where distance $A B=x$. The boy at $B$ stars running perpendicular to $A B$ with velocity $V_1$. The boy at A starts running simultaneously with velocity v and meets the other boy in time $t$. The value of $t$ is
questions.solution:
Let the initial position of boy A be the origin $(0,0)$ and boy B be at $(x,0)$, with boy B running perpendicular to AB with velocity $V_1$.

At time $t$, boy B's position is given by $(x, V_1 t)$, while boy A's position is $(v_x t, v_y t)$.

For the boys to meet, their positions must be equal: $(v_x t, v_y t) = (x, V_1 t)$, yielding $v_x = x/t$ and $v_y = V_1$.

The magnitude constraint $v^2 = v_x^2 + v_y^2$ becomes $v^2 = (x/t)^2 + V_1^2$.

Solving for $t$ gives $t^2 = x^2/(v^2 - V_1^2)$, requiring $v > V_1$ for real values.

The expression matches option C.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body when projected at an angle ' $\theta$ ' with the horizontal reaches a maximum height ' H '. The time of flight of the body will be (g=$ acceleration due to gravity)$
questions.solution:
Time of flight in terms of maximum height

The maximum height $H$ and time of flight $T$ for a projectile with initial velocity $u$ at angle $\theta$ are given by:

$H = \frac{u^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g}$

$T = \frac{2u \sin\theta}{g}$

From the height equation, $u^2 \sin^2\theta = 2gH$, so $u \sin\theta = \sqrt{2gH}$.

Substituting into the time equation yields:

$T = \frac{2}{g} \cdot \sqrt{2gH} = 2\sqrt{\frac{2H}{g}}$

This corresponds to option C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An inextensible string of length ' $\ell$ ' fixed at one end, carries a mass ' m ' at the other end. If the string makes $\frac{1}{\pi}$ revolutions per second around the vertical axis through the fixed end, the tension in the string is [The string makes an angle $\theta$ with the vertical]
questions.solution:
Conical pendulum analysis

The mass experiences tension $T$ along the string and gravitational force $mg$ downward.
Resolving tension into components: vertical component $T \cos\theta$ balances gravity, giving $T \cos\theta = mg$.

The horizontal component $T \sin\theta$ provides centripetal force for circular motion with radius $r = l \sin\theta$.

Given frequency $f = \frac{1}{\pi}$, angular frequency becomes $\omega = 2\pi f = 2$ rad/s.
Centripetal force is $F_c = m\omega^2 r = m(2)^2(l \sin\theta) = 4ml \sin\theta$.

Equating horizontal forces: $T \sin\theta = 4ml \sin\theta$.
Since $\sin\theta \neq 0$, dividing yields $T = 4ml$.

$\boxed{4ml}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two stones of masses m and 3 m are whirled in horizontal circles, the heavier one in a radius $\left(\frac{\mathrm{r}}{3}\right)$ and lighter one in a radius r . The tangential speed of lighter stone is ' $n$ ' times the value of heavier stone. When the magnitude of centripetal force becomes equal the value of $n$ is
questions.solution:
The centripetal forces are equal: $F_L = F_H$. For stones with masses $m_L = m$, $m_H = 3m$ and radii $r_L = r$, $r_H = \frac{r}{3}$, with tangential speeds related by $v_L = n v_H$, the force equality becomes:

$\frac{m (n v_H)^2}{r} = \frac{3m v_H^2}{r/3}$

Simplifying both sides yields:

$\frac{m n^2 v_H^2}{r} = \frac{9m v_H^2}{r}$

Answer: $\boxed{3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A vehicle is moving with a constant speed of $10 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$ in a circular horizontal track of radius 20 m. A bob is suspended from the roof of a vehicle by a massless string. The angle made by the string with the vertical will be (acceleration due to gravity, $g=10 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ )
questions.solution:
A vehicle moving at constant speed in a circular horizontal track establishes a centripetal acceleration, causing the suspended bob to make an angle $\theta$ with the vertical. The bob's mass is $m$ and the tension in the string is $T$.

For vertical equilibrium, the vertical component of tension balances the gravitational force: $T \cos\theta = mg$.

The horizontal component provides the centripetal force for circular motion: $T \sin\theta = \frac{mv^2}{r}$.

Dividing the horizontal equation by the vertical equation eliminates $T$ and $m: \frac{T \sin\theta}{T \cos\theta} = \frac{mv^2/r}{mg}$, which simplifies to $\tan\theta = \frac{v^2}{rg}$.

Substituting the given values $v = 10\,\text{m/s}$, $r = 20\,\text{m}$, and $g = 10\,\text{m/s}^2$ yields $\tan\theta = \frac{10^2}{20 \times 10} = 0.5$.

Therefore $\theta = \tan^{-1}(0.5)$, and the correct option is A.

The acceleration vector points to the centre of the circle.

B: The acceleration vector points radially inward as centripetal acceleration, not tangent to the circle. Only a tangential acceleration component would exist if angular speed were changing, which it is not.

C: Since velocity is tangent and acceleration is radial, they are perpendicular at every point.

D: Uniform circular motion produces purely centripetal acceleration directed toward the circle's center.

Statement B is false.

questions.solution:
when a body is revolving around a circular path, it experiences 2 forces: Centrifugal force and Centripetal Force.
Centrifugal force (Latin for 'center fleeing') describes the tendency of an object following a curved path to fly outwards, away from the center of the curve. It's not really a force; it results from inertia \(-\) the tendency of an object to resist any change in its state of rest or motion.
Centripetal force is a real force that counteracts the centrifugal force and prevents the object from 'flying out,' keeping it moving instead with a uniform speed along a circular path.
Centripetal force: \($\mathrm{Fc}=\frac{m v^{2}}{\mathrm{r}}$\)
Where as tangential force \(F_{t}=0 \Longrightarrow a_{t}=0\)
